_strings.@@a02b244cbdfa: Credit for Income Tax Paid to Another State or Country — N.C. residents (and part-year residents for the resident period) only. Available when income earned while a legal resident of North Carolina is taxed by both North Carolina and another U.S. state or a foreign country because it was earned in or derived from sources in that other state/country. No credit for tax paid to a city/county/other political subdivision or to the federal government. Nonresidents are NOT entitled to this credit. A copy of the return filed with the other state/country and proof of payment must be attached (the 2024 D-401 "What You Should Send Us" list requires a copy of the other state's return when the credit is claimed on Form D-400TC, Part 1, Line 7a).
_strings.@@a6c77a7280fd: Treaty conformity — NC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: NC conforms. The 2024 D-401 instructions state on Line 6: "The starting point for determining North Carolina taxable income is federal adjusted gross income" (IRC as of January 1, 2023 — the 2024 booklet keeps the January 1, 2023 conformity date). Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI, it flows through to NC untaxed UNLESS NC adds it back. The Form D-400 Schedule S, Part A "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" list in the 2024 D-401 (Lines 1-16: non-NC state/local bond interest, Opportunity Fund deferred gains, 85% bonus depreciation, 85% of the IRC 179 difference, S-corp built-in gains, federal-over-state basis on 2024 dispositions, federal NOL, pass-through state/local/foreign income tax under IRC 164, non-qualifying N.C. 529 withdrawals, discharge of qualified principal residence indebtedness, employer education-loan payments under IRC 127(c), expenses allocable to exempt income, discharge of certain student loan debt, etc.) contains NO add-back of treaty-exempt income. Since treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed, conforms_to_federal_treaties = true. Note one nuance to flag for filers: Schedule S Part A Line 12 requires adding back EXPENSES allocable to income exempt from NC tax, but it does not add back the exempt income itself.

_strings.@@de57f30661b2: Tax Credit for Rehabilitating Historic Structures (Articles 3D / 3H / 3L) — Narrow / not broadly applicable to ordinary residents. Available to taxpayers who incur qualified rehabilitation expenditures/expenses on a certified historic structure or historic mill facility under Article 3D, Article 3H (historic mill facility), or Article 3L (Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credits Investment Program; requires Form NC-Rehab attached to the front of Form D-400). Tax line: D-400 Line 15: multiply Line 14 (N.C. taxable income, full-year residents) by the income tax rate of 4.5% (0.0450) — printed on the 2024 form: "Multiply Line 14 by 4.5% (0.0450). If zero or less, enter a zero." Line 6 starts from federal AGI; Line 14 = federal AGI + additions - deductions - child deduction (Line 10) - N.C. standard/itemized deduction (Line 11). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change: the individual income tax rate dropped to 4.5% (0.0450) for tax year 2024 (from 4.75% in 2023) — 2024 D-401 "What is the Tax Rate?"; the standard deduction chart is unchanged from 2023. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled by calc.state_tax: MFS gets $0 if the spouse itemizes, and the N.C. standard deduction is ZERO for anyone not eligible for the FEDERAL standard deduction (see federal Pub 501; the filing chart lists nonresident aliens at $0) — itemizers use D-400 Line 11 itemized deductions (Form D-400 Schedule A) instead; compute those cases on the form. N.C. child deduction (D-400 Line 10) is NOT modeled: up to $3,000 per qualifying child (a child for whom the federal child tax credit was allowed), stepping down $3,000/$2,500/$2,000/$1,500/$1,000/$500/$0 by federal AGI (MFJ/QSS brackets up to $40,000 ... over $140,000; HoH up to $30,000 ... over $105,000; Single/MFS up to $20,000 ... over $70,000) — the 2024 D-401 Child Deduction Table is unchanged from 2023; take it from the worksheet, not from a per-dependent exemption. North Carolina has no personal or dependent exemptions.
